content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a transformer-based model human pose estimation and mesh reconstruction, which attempts to preserve the spatial structure when modeling self-attention in the transformer blocks. While the input to vanilla transformers is flatten, the main idea in this paper is to map the input features to three matrices corresponding the query, key, and value, then implementing the multi-head self-attention module for matrices rather than vectors.  In addition, the self-attention module is decomposed to two streams, representing the two spatial dimensions, and therefore its overall complexity is reduced. The proposed model outperforms SOTA methods on the 3.6M dataset while being more efficient.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

(*) SOTA methods such as MeshGraphormer and METRO architectures are based on vanilla transformers and require computational cost. The decomposition of spatial dimension seems to significantly reduce memory compared with these models. 

(*) The proposed masking strategy is interesting and seems to improve the robustness of the estimated 3D pose. 

(*) The model outperforms SOTA methods on the major benchmark for mesh reconstruction and human pose estimation. 

Weaknesses:

(*) Few recent papers (e.g., Swin-Transformer and ConvNextT models) also discussed ideas to preserve spatial structure of transformers, and to reduce number of parameters. Although they were not directly designed for the HPE or mesh reconstruction tasks, but as backbones for classification, detection, and segmentation, I was hoping to see some discussion comparing your model with those.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clear. Novelty is somewhat limited. Most parts seem to be reproducible.
content.summary_of_the_review: Few modifications to vanilla transformers, yet clearly outperforms SOTA methods on major benchmarks.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a method for 2D/3D pose estimation from an image with a single person. To loosen the heavy computational requirement of Transformer, it proposes to learn the self-attention in the 2D feature space, which allows converting the fully connected computation to convolution that needs fewer resources. Feature map reconstruction module augments the data by dropping off the features for random keypoints to simulate the occlusions. In experiments, the proposed method shows comparable results to other methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+ Lightweight neural network that uses small amount of resources. Since the proposed transformers are free from fully connected computation, the required memory is small, allowing practical use in real-world applications.
+ The data augmentation strategy (i.e., feature map reconstruction) is a practical solution to simulate various occlusion cases, leading to good generalizability. 


Weakness:
- Weak problem formulation. The research problem introduced in this paper, i.e., improving computational time, is not interesting since many existing methods have already shown convincing computational efficiency even for multiple people, e.g., openpose. Improving a real-time model into super-real-time does not sound appealing research problem.
- The novelty of this paper is highly lacking. The weakness in problem formulation naturally propagates to novelty: 1) saving the computational cost by preserving 2D spatial dimension is too obvious, and it still loses global relationship (which is counterintuitive of the goal of Transformer) that sacrifices the accuracy (based on the comparison between VanillaTransformer_L and FeatER in Table 4); 2) feature map reconstruction module is actually playing the same role as drop-off augmentation, which significantly drops the excitement of the paper.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Misleading claim: 
In page2, “FeatER ensures that the self-attention is conducted based on the original 2D feature maps, which is more structurally meaningful”; and “This is less than ideal for preserving the structural context of the feature maps during the refinement stage”: why is exciting Transformer less structurally meaningful and less ideal for preserving the structural context? These sentences need more clarification since existing transformer-based approaches also somehow capture both the spatial and global relationship.
content.summary_of_the_review:
While this paper is successful to improve computational efficiency, the novelty is highly lacking with weak research problem formulation. This paper needs a strong justification for why computational efficiency should be still improved in 2D/3D human pose estimation field by sacrificing the accuracy where existing methods have already shown good computational performance.

I also would like to note that it was hard for me to make rich comments not because the paper is very clear but because the contributions are quite lacking (with respect to novelty).

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a Transformer-based 2D/3D human pose estimation system, called FeatER. FeatER takes feature maps, extracted by CNN-based backbone, and refines the feature maps with a Transformer-based module. The refined feature maps are used for downstream tasks, such as 2D/3D human pose estimation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
Experimental results show that the proposed FeatER is greatly helpful for both effective and efficient 2D/3D human pose estimation.

Weaknesses
The proposed system uses HybrIK as a final mesh regressor (Section 4.1). However, with the same mesh regressor, the original HybrIK performs much better on 3DPW regardless of using 3DPW training set. See Table 2 of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2011.14672.pdf. The gap becomes very large when 3DPW is not used during the training stage. HybrIK without 3DPW achieves PA MPJPE 48.8, MPJPE 80.0, and MPVPE 94.5, while FeatER achieves PA MPJPE 54.5, MPJPE 88.4, and MPVPE 105.6. Given similarity between 3DPW training and testing sets, performance without using 3DPW training set reflects performance of methods in the wild better than using it. Human3.6M suffers from the same similarity as training and testing sets of Human3.6M are captured from the same studio and same camera viewpoints. Hence, 3D errors on 3DPW without using 3DPW as a training set is a major metric. On such a major metric, FeatER performs worse than HybrIK although FeatER uses the 3D mesh regression module of HybrIK. Although FeatER requires a smaller number of parameters and MACs, the gap seems not very large given the large 3D errors gap.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Efficiency of FeatER is noticeable. Given a promise for releasing codes, stated in the abstract, the method could be produced.
content.summary_of_the_review: FeatER is an efficient and effective system for 2D/3D human pose estimation. The efficiency part is impressive for me. However, given the same module, it performs somewhat worse than HybrIK. Although there are some computational costs gaps, the gap seems not very large considering a large 3D errors gap.

content.title: FeatER: An Efficient Network for Human Reconstruction Feature map-based TransformER
content.abstract: Recently, vision transformers have shown great success in a set of human reconstruction tasks such as 2D human pose estimation (2D HPE), 3D human pose estimation (3D HPE), and human mesh reconstruction (HMR) tasks. In these tasks, feature map representations of the human structural information are often extracted first from the image by a CNN (such as HRNet), and then further processed by transformer to predict the heatmaps (encodes each joint's location into a feature map with a Gaussian distribution) for HPE or HMR. However, existing transformer architectures are not able to process these feature map inputs directly, forcing an unnatural flattening of the location-sensitive human structural information. Furthermore, much of the performance benefit in recent HPE and HMR methods has come at the cost of ever-increasing computation and memory needs. Therefore, to simultaneously address these problems, we propose FeatER, a novel transformer design which preserves the inherent structure of feature map representations when modeling attention while reducing the memory and computational costs. Taking advantage of FeatER, we build an efficient network for a set of human reconstruction tasks including 2D HPE, 3D HPE, and HMR. A feature map reconstruction module is applied to improve the performance of the estimated human pose and mesh. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of FeatER on various human pose and mesh datasets. For instance, FeatER outperforms the SOTA method MeshGraphormer by requiring 5\% of Params (total parameters) and 16\% of MACs (the Multiply–Accumulate Operations) on Human3.6M and 3DPW datasets. Code will be publicly available.
